name: Buddhistisches Zentrum Scheibbs
aka: Verein der Freunde des Buddhistischen Kultur- und Meditationszentrums Scheibbs
tradition: Non-sectarian Buddhist retreat house spanning Zen, Theravada/Vipassana, and Vajrayana, taught by a rotating roster of lay and monastic teachers rather than a single resident lineage
technique: Silent sitting and walking meditation across Zen, Vipassana, and Vajrayana forms, plus a daily work period
influences: Santacitta Bhikkhuni / Amaravati Theravada forest tradition
teacherAccess: Each retreat is led by a visiting teacher with daily group sitting and instruction or Dharma talks; the format (personal interviews, small groups) varies by teacher and tradition
retreatOptions: Weekly open meditation evenings (Thu/Sun); weekend and long-weekend seminars; residential retreats typically 3 to 10 nights across Zen, Vipassana, and Vajrayana
about: Buddhistisches Zentrum Scheibbs (BZS) is an independent, lay-run Buddhist retreat house in Neustift, on a wooded hillside above the Erlauf river near Scheibbs in Lower Austria. It was founded in 1975 by a group of Vienna-based Buddhists in a former sanatorium of the Austrian Association for the Blind, inside a building whose history stretches back to a 16th-century ironworks hammer mill, making it one of Austria's oldest dedicated meditation centres. Rather than following one lineage or resident teacher, BZS runs a year-round programme of retreats spanning Zen, Vipassana, and Vajrayana, led by a rotating roster of Austrian and international teachers, including Zen priest Edward Espe Brown, Theravada forest nun Santacitta Bhikkhuni, and long-time Vipassana teachers such as Ursula Lyon and Hannes Huber. Retreats run from weekend introductions up to roughly ten-night intensives, combining largely silent group sitting and walking meditation with a daily work period, in a house that sleeps around forty guests in shared, single, and double rooms. The centre is supported by a non-profit membership association; house costs cover board and lodging, while teaching for many courses is offered on a dana (voluntary donation) basis paid directly to the visiting teacher.
schedule: Multi-day retreats begin with a shared evening meal and run a daily schedule of group sitting, walking meditation, and a work period, ending after lunch on the final day; largely silent throughout
cost: Course fee (Kursgebühr) for teaching is either a fixed amount or Dana (voluntary donation, paid in cash at the course, never by bank transfer); separate house costs (Hauskosten, covering board and lodging) are billed per stay at a standard daily rate, plus optional single/double room surcharges and a bed-linen fee

pricePerDay.notes: 10-night Vipassana Retreat (5-15 Nov 2026): Hauskosten (board & lodging) of EUR 770 total = EUR 77/night in a shared multi-bed room; +EUR 18/night single-room surcharge = EUR 95/night (a single room with private bath adds EUR 28/night instead). Figures exclude the separate Dana teaching fee (suggested minimum EUR 750 for this retreat), which the site's own pricing page treats as distinct from Hauskosten.

foodNotes: Lacto-vegetarian full board (three meals plus all-day fruit, herbal/black/green tea, coffee, and juice); vegan or medically-necessary special diets available on request for a small surcharge; produce partly from the centre's own garden and organic or free-range suppliers.
workNotes: A rotating small group of guests assists the kitchen team during the daily work period as part of the practice; the centre describes work meditation as part of many but not necessarily every retreat.
